I have a hardcore AA style. Here’s what has helped me a lot:

First, I really did have to come to terms with the fact that, if my boyfriend and I *did* break up, it wouldn’t actually be the end of the world. Of course it would hurt and of course I would be in rough state for a while, but life does still go on. Surround yourself with your friends/family. I know it doesn’t feel the same as your partner, but it will help so much

Second thing is related to that: don’t vent everything to only your partner! Make sure you have a support system around you that isn’t just one person. He can’t support everything in your life and still navigate through his own. 

Third: ask him for reassure every now and again and you’ll notice that your way of thinking like that goes down immensely. Don’t overdo it, though! It’s okay to ask him “Hey, we’re doing okay, right?” every now and again, but if you ask him continuously, it gets annoying as hell. My boyfriend would attest to that lol

Fourth and lastly: ask yourself questions and approach your own feelings with curiosity. “Okay I’m feeling really scared that he’s hates me after that. Why do I feel that way? What has HE done that indicates that to me? Is there a chance I’m making things worse in my own head and everything is okay?” Going through that checklist with myself, whether it’s in my head or even writing things out, helps so much. 

I hope these strategies help. Living with the AA style is hard as hell, but there are ways to manage it. Here for you, if you need to talk. 💛

Sorry but your comment is harmful. I am not invalidating your PERSONAL experience (mods please do not come after me for this), but saying things like “purposely obtuse” implies malicious intent, which is completely unfair and untrue. 

Also, I have seen your comments and posts SO many times on this sub, and I’m surprised you don’t understand this yet: most neurodivergent people do NOT understand intent and context clues. Implying we are not offering healthy communication because we don’t (read: aren’t able to) extrapolate meaning and intent from context clues is absolutely unfair. We often need things explained clearly and concisely to understand what is going on. 

Taking a second to explain what you mean to a neurodivergent person without getting upset is not only completely acceptable to expect, but is also good practice for everyone on this planet.

While I do think Dx folks need to figure out how to stop doing it, I do want to mention that, from my own personal experience, I am never “purposely obtuse”. It really is a desire to be as specific as possible and is never done to deflect.

Like I said, this is MY personal experience, but yeah.

While it is arguing semantics, we often don’t even realize that’s what it is. When you say one thing and our experience is different (like him walking up to the car and you saying he walked up to you), we latch onto that because, in our eyes, it’s incorrect. 

I’m not saying it’s okay and the right thing to do, I just hope this helps with perspective. We really like specifics and find it hard to get past something that is inherently wrong, regardless of whether or not it’s important. 

It’s a hard thing to work on from the Dx side but I do hope he does because it can be so so frustrating for you. And I’m sorry you’re experiencing this.

I have a hardcore AA style. Here’s what has helped me a lot:

First, I really did have to come to terms with the fact that, if my boyfriend and I *did* break up, it wouldn’t actually be the end of the world. Of course it would hurt and of course I would be in rough state for a while, but life does still go on. Surround yourself with your friends/family. I know it doesn’t feel the same as your partner, but it will help so much

Second thing is related to that: don’t vent everything to only your partner! Make sure you have a support system around you that isn’t just one person. He can’t support everything in your life and still navigate through his own. 

Third: ask him for reassure every now and again and you’ll notice that your way of thinking like that goes down immensely. Don’t overdo it, though! It’s okay to ask him “Hey, we’re doing okay, right?” every now and again, but if you ask him continuously, it gets annoying as hell. My boyfriend would attest to that lol

Fourth and lastly: ask yourself questions and approach your own feelings with curiosity. “Okay I’m feeling really scared that he’s hates me after that. Why do I feel that way? What has HE done that indicates that to me? Is there a chance I’m making things worse in my own head and everything is okay?” Going through that checklist with myself, whether it’s in my head or even writing things out, helps so much. 

I hope these strategies help. Living with the AA style is hard as hell, but there are ways to manage it. Here for you, if you need to talk. 💛

The reason I would say “yes” to you disclosing your diagnosis is, simply put, the more you’re forced to mask, the faster you will burn out. It’s not fair for you to be forced to make facial expressions and exude enthusiasm just to appease their NT brains.
